rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
The greater one-horned rhino is protected in Chitwan and Bardia. Its global rank is Vulnerable, after a recovery from a very small population.
The Bengal tiger is Endangered. Nepal's Terai parks hold the breeding population.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Endangered (EN) vs endemic:** endangered describes extinction risk; endemic describes geographic restriction (the spiny babbler is endemic to Nepal but Least Concern).  ·  **Umbrella vs keystone species:** umbrella species protect others through large habitat needs (tiger); keystone species have outsized ecological roles (elephants as habitat engineers).

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **The umbrella effect:** one large-habitat flagship (tiger) pulls an entire ecosystem under protection — efficient conservation.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Nepal's threatened species: gharial CR (rivers); tiger, red panda, arna EN; rhino, snow leopard VU; Bengal florican CR (grasslands).  ·  Success: rhino ~100 (1960s) → 750+; tigers 121 (2009) → 355 (2022) — Tx2 met early. Caution: gharial recruitment low; arna hybridisation.  ·  Flagship/umbrella logic: conserving tiger landscapes shelters whole communities.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Nepal met the international Tx2 goal — doubling tigers — ahead of the 2022 deadline, one of the few countries to do so.

Fundamental Concepts **Endangered species** are species facing a very high risk of extinction in the wild (IUCN EN), often used loosely for all threatened species (CR, EN, VU).
